minutes.headline: Committee approved two sidewalk letters, tabled the protocol review, and deferred bus policy pending cost and capacity numbers.
minutes.summary: The meeting covered back-to-school reports, the FY24 budget timeline and an invitation from the Finance Committee, and two letters urging sidewalks near schools. Members reassigned committee seats after a new member joined, and discussed busing after the suspended transportation policy led to 214 new requests. The superintendent was asked to study the feasibility and cost of busing all students, with the policy to return to a later agenda.

public_comment.topic: Supported the committee's transportation policy; suggested bus fees and criticised parents who went to social media.
Asked about a crossing guard on 2A, sidewalk clearing by DPW in winter, and school closures in extreme cold.
Questioned the bus driver incident, the adequacy of one athletic trainer, and the sustainability of five-year budget planning.
Said busing is not always better for high school students because of long ride times.
A parent asked whether DPW had been contacted about clearing sidewalks in winter.

votes.motion: Approve the letter to the Select Board on sidewalks, as amended.
Approve the letter to state legislators on sidewalks, as amended in discussion.
Approve the adjustments to the committee organization chart and assignments.
Table the protocol review to the next meeting.

decisions.decision: The superintendent will work with the Finance Committee chair on how to respond to the invitation; the five-year staffing plan stays on the December schedule.
The superintendent is to study whether busing all students is feasible and what it would cost, then bring numbers back; transportation goes on the next agenda.
The committee will find the last date a bus can be ordered and work the policy timeline backward from it.
The protocol review will be voted at the next meeting, with an edit to the public-meeting sentence.
Transportation policy will be discussed by the whole committee first, then go to the policy subcommittee for drafting and three readings.
The new member will fill vacated committee roles, including the high school council and lifelong learning advisory.
Superintendent goals are on the next meeting's agenda, with approval of the student learning goal sought that night.

what_happened.line: The committee deferred bus policy and asked the superintendent to study whether busing all students is feasible and what it would cost, with transportation on the next agenda.
Members voted on two letters urging sidewalks near schools, one to the Select Board and one to state legislators, both as amended; the tally was not audible.
The protocol review was tabled to the next meeting, to be voted with an edit to the public-meeting sentence.
The committee will find the last date a bus can be ordered and work the policy timeline backward from it.
The superintendent will work with the Finance Committee chair on responding to its invitation; the five-year staffing plan stays on the December schedule.

why_it_matters: Members said an additional bus would have to be paid from the existing school budget, so any busing expansion competes with other school lines unless a fee or new money is found.
The sidewalk letters ask other bodies to act; members noted DPW sidewalk money covers repair of existing sidewalks, not new ones, so the letters do not themselves fund anything.
watch_next: The next School Committee agenda: transportation numbers from the superintendent, the protocol review vote, and approval of the student learning goal.
The bus-order deadline the committee is to find, which sets the timeline for the transportation policy.
